fields.description:
## Context / Problem

Even with schema-filtered selection (the selection story this depends on), extraction from
free text stays heuristic: a trailing schema-valid decoy can win, and models fence-wrap quoted
JSON so fences cannot serve as the channel (measured: E2 catch 2, experiment-results comment
on the selection bug). An explicit output channel makes the payload location a stated contract
instead of an inference.

## Approach

Extend `schema_directive` (src/rebar/llm/structured.py:75) to instruct the model to wrap its
single final JSON object between the literal markers `<<<REBAR_OUTPUT>>>` and `<<<END>>>`.

Extraction is added to `parse_structured` (src/rebar/llm/structured.py:301) as an EXPLICIT
block-ordered wrapper around the existing selection logic. First, factor the current
`parse_structured` body (`_candidate_dicts` -> `validate_to` (:189) -> last-valid-wins ->
raise-last-error / `tolerant_parse` fallthrough) into a private helper
`_select_and_validate(text, model_cls)`. Then `parse_structured` becomes: scan the reply for
COMPLETE marker blocks (a `<<<REBAR_OUTPUT>>>` paired with a later `<<<END>>>`) in DOCUMENT order;
if there is >= 1 block, iterate the blocks in REVERSE (last-first) and return the first
`_select_and_validate(block_content, model_cls)` that yields a validated object; if NONE of the
blocks yields one, RAISE the LAST (document-order) block's validation error (fail-closed). If
there are ZERO complete blocks, return `_select_and_validate(full_reply, model_cls)` — byte-for-
byte today's behavior.

Why the explicit reverse-iteration and NOT "concatenate the marker regions and run the pipeline
once" (a subtlety the review flagged): `_candidate_dicts` does NOT preserve document order — it
emits ALL fenced-block candidates first, then every balanced top-level object, then the whole-
text candidate — so the pipeline's own "last validated wins" is NOT the same as "last marker
BLOCK wins". Iterating blocks last-first and delegating WITHIN each block to `_select_and_validate`
makes the cross-block last-block-wins guarantee explicit and independent of `_candidate_dicts`'
internal ordering, while still inheriting df3a's per-block schema-filtered selection and
tolerant-repair recovery verbatim. `_select_and_validate` runs on a single block's content, so
there is no re-entrancy into marker extraction.

Failure/fall-through rule (mirrors df3a, made explicit — this is the boundary the review flagged):

- Markers PRESENT (>= 1 complete block): iterate blocks last-first; the first block whose content
  yields a validated object via `_select_and_validate` wins (explicit last-block-wins).
- Markers PRESENT, a block's content needs json-repair (trailing comma, unclosed brace, smart
  quotes, fence-wrapped object inside the block): `_select_and_validate` applies the SAME
  `tolerant_parse` recovery df3a applies, scoped to that block — so repair behavior is inherited,
  not reinvented.
- Markers PRESENT but NO block yields a validated object even after repair: RAISE the LAST
  (document-order) block's validation error (df3a's "raise the LAST one's error", fail-closed). It
  does NOT fall through to a full-reply selection — a reply that USED the channel but produced
  invalid content must fail-closed rather than let a decoy OUTSIDE the markers win. This is the
  single bounded-retry signal (layer 4), identical to df3a.
- Markers ABSENT, or an opening `<<<REBAR_OUTPUT>>>` with NO closing `<<<END>>>` (an incomplete
  block is treated as no complete block): `_select_and_validate(full_reply)` — byte-for-byte
  today's behavior, so df3a-era and non-compliant-model transcripts are unaffected.

The directive literal is SINGLE-SOURCED as a module constant in structured.py (e.g.
`SENTINEL_DIRECTIVE`, naming both markers) so exactly one string is used by `schema_directive`,
by the marker extractor, and by the measurement harness — no drift between what the model is
told and what the parser looks for. The first-attempt append at src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py:211-212
(`schema_hint = structured.schema_directive(model_cls)`) is unchanged in MECHANISM — it still
appends `schema_directive`'s output, which now carries the markers. But the BOUNDED-RETRY prompt
at structured_run.py:236-241 re-appends `schema_hint` AND then adds a standalone trailing
instruction — "Reply with ONLY the JSON object matching the schema above — no prose, no code
fence." — that omits the markers and tells the model to emit BARE JSON, contradicting the marker
directive on precisely the fail-closed retry that layer 4 depends on. This story fixes that
contradiction: the retry tail is single-sourced from (or updated to name) the same markers, so
the retry says "wrap that one object between `<<<REBAR_OUTPUT>>>` and `<<<END>>>` — no prose, no
code fence", keeping the channel consistent across both attempts.

Marker-pairing rule (review finding — repeated/interleaved markers): pairing is a single
left-to-right, non-nested scan. Each `<<<REBAR_OUTPUT>>>` pairs with the NEXT `<<<END>>>` that
follows it; scanning then resumes AFTER that `<<<END>>>`. So OPEN...OPEN...END yields ONE block
(the first OPEN with the END; the inner OPEN is literal text inside the block), OPEN...END...
OPEN...END yields TWO blocks (last wins), and a trailing OPEN with no following END contributes
NO complete block. No nesting, no overlap — the rule is total and deterministic for any marker
sequence.

Rollback / sequencing (review finding): no feature flag is introduced, and that is safe by
construction — (a) the extraction side is byte-for-byte identical to today for any reply with no
complete marker block, so markerless/legacy transcripts cannot regress; (b) the ONLY live
behavior change is the directive's effect on model output, which AC5 MEASURES per cell (before/
after, in the harness) as a close precondition, so a per-cell regression is caught BEFORE the
change is submitted, not after; (c) the change is a single atomic Gerrit change — if a
post-merge regression is later observed, it reverts as one commit. If AC5 shows a per-cell
parse-success regression, the story does not close and the change is held/reverted rather than
shipped.

Instruction-locality reconciliation (review finding): `schema_directive`'s existing literal says
"ONLY a single JSON object ... no prose, no markdown fence". The marker instruction does NOT
contradict it — `<<<REBAR_OUTPUT>>>`/`<<<END>>>` are literal SENTINEL lines, not prose and not a
markdown code fence. The single-sourced constant states this explicitly: still exactly one JSON
object, still no prose and no ``` fence; ADDITIONALLY, place that one object between the two
literal marker lines. So one prompt string carries a single, non-conflicting instruction.

Directive and extraction land in ONE change, deliberately: E2 measured that shipping the
directive alone flips quote-in-prose from 0% to 100% and breaks the current parser 10/10 — a
split would leave the system broken between changes. The marker literal is the E2-tested one
(16/16 channel compliance across sonnet/haiku on Bedrock, 0/26 decoy wins). Prior art:
Anthropic's answer-tag extraction guidance and aider's `<<<`-style sentinel blocks; markdown
fences are disqualified as the channel because models fence-wrap quoted material (E2).

The a40f harness currently appends a PLACEHOLDER directive
(tests/external/test_structured_output_matrix.py `_SENTINEL_DIRECTIVE`, whose own comment says
"the sentinel story (a sibling) owns refining it"); this story replaces that placeholder with the
real single-sourced constant so the operator-attested before/after run (AC5) measures THIS
story's actual directive against the current parser, not a prototype.

## Scope

- src/rebar/llm/structured.py — the single-sourced `SENTINEL_DIRECTIVE` constant (with the
  reconciled "single object, no prose/fence, wrapped between the two marker lines" wording, and a
  docstring that is the durable home of the marker-channel contract) and its inclusion in
  `schema_directive` (:75); factor the current `parse_structured` (:301) body into a private
  `_select_and_validate(text, model_cls)` helper, and rewrite `parse_structured` as the marker
  wrapper: last-first block iteration over `_select_and_validate` when complete blocks exist,
  else `_select_and_validate(full_reply)` unchanged
- src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py — update the bounded-retry trailing instruction (:236-241) to
  name the markers (single-sourced with `SENTINEL_DIRECTIVE`), so the fail-closed retry that
  layer 4 depends on instructs the SAME channel as the first attempt; the first-attempt append
  (:211-212) is unchanged in mechanism
- docs/adr/ — a short ADR recording the sentinel marker-channel as a durable output-channel
  contract (the markers, the last-block-wins + fail-closed extraction rule, and why fences were
  rejected), so the architectural decision persists beyond this plan body
- tests/external/test_structured_output_matrix.py — replace the placeholder `_SENTINEL_DIRECTIVE`
  with the single-sourced constant so the harness measures this story's real directive; the
  existing scorer (tests/external/_structured_matrix.py) and its oracle are UNCHANGED (AC5 uses
  the existing `new_ok`/`n`/`layout_counts` non-regression measurement)
- tests/unit/test_structured.py — marker pins, incl. the fenced-quote hazard pin and the
  malformed/incomplete-marker pins below
- tests/fixtures/ — E2 sentinel replies added to the corpus

## Testing

Unit/contract tier (real reply text through the real parser):

- Marker extraction pins: one block; multiple blocks -> LAST wins; markerless -> selection
  fallback yields the identical result (parameterized contrast against the selection story's
  tests); marker block containing a fenced object -> payload still wins.
- The fenced-quote hazard pin: a fence-wrapped schema-decoy plus a marker-wrapped payload ->
  the marker payload wins (regression pin for E2 catch 2).
- Marker-first ordering pin: a reply carrying BOTH a marker-wrapped valid payload AND an
  earlier schema-valid decoy object parses to the MARKER payload (markers beat the selection
  pipeline). Mutation check: dropping marker priority (extraction ignores markers, or runs the
  selection pipeline over the full reply first) turns this and the E2-reply corpus test RED.
- Malformed/incomplete-marker pins (the review-flagged boundary):
  - An opening `<<<REBAR_OUTPUT>>>` with NO closing `<<<END>>>` -> treated as markerless: the
    full-reply selection pipeline runs and yields today's result.
  - Repeated/interleaved markers: OPEN...OPEN...END -> ONE block; OPEN...END...OPEN...END ->
    TWO blocks (last wins); trailing OPEN with no END -> contributes no block. Pins the
    left-to-right, next-close, non-nested pairing rule.
  - A marker block whose content needs json-repair (trailing comma / unclosed brace) ->
    repaired via the inherited tolerant_parse path, scoped to the marker region.
  - A marker block whose content is schema-INVALID with a valid schema-decoy OUTSIDE the markers
    -> RAISES StructuredOutputError (fail-closed); it does NOT fall through and pick the outside
    decoy. Mutation check: making the invalid-marker case fall through to full-reply selection
    turns this RED.
- Bounded-retry consistency pin: after a first-attempt parse failure, the retry prompt built in
  structured_run.py names the markers (no "bare JSON / no fence" instruction that omits them), so
  the retry channel matches the first attempt. Mutation check: reverting the retry tail to the
  markerless wording turns this RED.
- Markerless regression pin: a reply with NO markers yields the IDENTICAL result the
  schema-filtered selection pipeline produces today (byte-for-byte fall-through), so df3a-era and
  non-compliant-model transcripts are unaffected.
- LLM-surface evidence is measured by the harness (test-design §10: paired directives, fixed n,
  deterministic scoring) and recorded here as an operator-attested artifact (AC5).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The directive names both markers, reconciled with the "single object, no prose/fence"
      clause (markers are sentinels, not a fence), and extraction honors them with
      last-block-wins — checked by the new unit pins in tests/unit/test_structured.py.
- [ ] A markerless reply, AND an unterminated opening marker with no close, both fall back to
      schema-filtered full-reply selection with identical results; and repeated/interleaved
      markers pair by the stated left-to-right next-close rule (OPEN...OPEN...END -> one block;
      OPEN...END...OPEN...END -> two, last wins) — checked by parameterized contrast/boundary
      tests.
- [ ] The bounded-retry prompt (structured_run.py) names the markers rather than instructing
      bare JSON, so the fail-closed retry channel matches the first attempt — checked by the
      retry-consistency pin.
- [ ] A fence-wrapped decoy alongside a marker-wrapped payload parses to the payload — checked
      by the pinned hazard test.
- [ ] A reply carrying a marker-wrapped valid payload AND an EARLIER plain schema-valid decoy
      object parses to the marker payload; and a reply whose marker block is schema-INVALID
      while a valid decoy sits OUTSIDE the markers RAISES (fail-closed) rather than selecting the
      outside decoy — checked by the marker-first ordering + malformed-marker pins in
      tests/unit/test_structured.py.
- [ ] [operator-attested] A harness before/after run (old placeholder directive vs the real
      single-sourced SENTINEL_DIRECTIVE) shows, PER CELL, that parse success (the existing
      scorer's `new_ok/n`) does NOT REGRESS versus the a40f-inherited baseline, and improves on
      the cells whose failures were location/decoy/prose-driven. This uses the EXISTING scorer
      (`ScoreTable`: `new_ok`/`n` + `layout_counts`) unchanged — no new scorer fields — so no
      edits to tests/external/_structured_matrix.py or its offline oracle are needed.
      The channel's two deterministic guarantees are proven OFFLINE, not by a paid live run:
      marker-first extraction / NO DECOY WINS is pinned by the unit tests above, and channel
      COMPLIANCE (models actually emit the markers) is the E2 measured fact (16/16 across
      sonnet/haiku on Bedrock). This story provides a reliable output CHANNEL; ABSOLUTE parse
      success is bounded above by CONTENT validity (a model emitting wrong keys/values), which a
      channel does not fix — the a40f run already measured ~55% parse success on anthropic/bedrock
      under a placeholder directive with layout ALREADY 100% prose, so those residual failures are
      content, not channel. Gating on an absolute >= 95% parse-success bar would mis-measure
      content-validity as if it were the channel's job; the honest close bar is per-cell
      non-regression (+ improvement where failures were channel-driven), and any residual content
      gap is recorded as discovered work, not a block. The artifact link is recorded as a comment
      on this ticket.
